record.paper_title: Concrete examples of the rate of convergence of Chernoff approximations: numerical results for the heat semigroup and open questions on them (with appendix: full list of pictures and Python code)
record.context_brief: Different xi-dependence for trigonometric and exponential data
record.original_question: For the heat equation u_t(t,x)=u_xx(t,x) on the real line, work in the Banach space UC_b(R) of bounded uniformly continuous real functions with the sup norm. Let Lf=f'' generate the heat semigroup e^{tL}. For t=1/2, compare the exact solution e^{tL}u0 with Chernoff products G(t/n)^n u0 and S(t/n)^n u0, where G is first-order Chernoff tangent to L and S is second-order Chernoff tangent to L. Write d_n^G=||e^{tL}u0-G(t/n)^n u0|| and d_n^S=||e^{tL}u0-S(t/n)^n u0||, and estimate log d_n approximately as alpha log n plus beta, where alpha is the order of decreasing error and beta is the free term. For initial conditions with smoothness parameter xi in [1,4.5], why does the trigonometric family u0(x)=|sin x|^xi exhibit an apparently linear dependence of alpha_S on xi but no comparable dependence of alpha_G on xi, while the exponential family u0(x)=exp(-|x|^xi) appears to show no dependence of either alpha_G or alpha_S on xi? What feature distinguishes the trigonometric and exponential families in the convergence-rate behavior of the first-order and second-order Chernoff approximations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the heat equation u_t(t,x) = u_{xx}(t,x) on the real line, posed in the Banach space F = UC_b(R) of bounded uniformly continuous functions f: R → R, equipped with the sup norm ||f|| = sup_{x in R} |f(x)|. Let L be the generator of the heat semigroup (e^{tL})_{t≥0} acting on F (so Lf = f'' on a suitable core). For each t ≥ 0 define the bounded linear operators

  (G(t)f)(x) = (1/2) f(x) + (1/4) f(x + 2 sqrt(t)) + (1/4) f(x - 2 sqrt(t)),
  (S(t)f)(x) = (2/3) f(x) + (1/6) f(x + sqrt(6 t)) + (1/6) f(x - sqrt(6 t)).

These satisfy G(0) = S(0) = I and are tangent to L at 0 of orders 1 and 2 respectively, so by Chernoff's theorem, for every fixed t > 0 and every u_0 in F,

  d_n^G := || e^{tL} u_0 - G(t/n)^n u_0 ||  →  0,
  d_n^S := || e^{tL} u_0 - S(t/n)^n u_0 ||  →  0  as n → ∞.

Fix t = 1/2 and model the asymptotic decay numerically by

  log d_n^G ≈ α_G log n + β_G,    log d_n^S ≈ α_S log n + β_S,

calling α the order of decreasing error and β the free term.

Consider two one-parameter families of initial data indexed by a smoothness parameter ξ ∈ [1, 4.5]:

  (Trigonometric family)  u_0(x) = |sin x|^ξ,
  (Exponential family)    u_0(x) = exp(-|x|^ξ).

Empirically one observes that:
 (i) For the trigonometric family, α_S depends approximately linearly on ξ, while α_G shows no comparable dependence on ξ.
 (ii) For the exponential family, neither α_G nor α_S depends appreciably on ξ.

Explain, with rigorous justification, this phenomenon: identify the structural feature distinguishing the two families that causes the order of decreasing error of the second-order Chernoff approximation to be sensitive to the smoothness parameter ξ in the trigonometric case but not in the exponential case, and that causes the order of decreasing error of the first-order Chernoff approximation to be insensitive to ξ in both cases. Equivalently, derive sharp asymptotic upper and lower bounds on d_n^G and d_n^S as n → ∞ for each family, expressed in terms of ξ, that account for the observed dependence (or absence thereof) of α_G and α_S on ξ.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open numerical/theoretical puzzle about the ξ-dependence of empirical convergence orders α_G, α_S of first- and second-order Chernoff approximations to the heat semigroup. No subsequent work appears to have rigorously explained the observed asymmetry between the trigonometric and exponential families; the problem is listed among open questions and no resolution has been located in the literature.
